own_scenes.desc: Bun B y Pimp C, de Port Arthur, se llamaron Underground Kingz porque creían que no gustarían fuera del Golfo. En Jive desde 1992, Too Hard to Swallow incluía «Pocket Full of Stones» (en Menace II Society); Bun pulió su lírica con Royal Flush y Pimp, hijo de un trompetista de blues, mezclaba zydeco, soul y G-funk: Ridin’ Dirty (1996), con samples de los Isley, Bootsy y Curtis Mayfield, grabado en VHS, fue la primera vez que el país oyó hablar de las cintas de Screw. Pimp C no quería «Big Pimpin’» con Jay-Z sobre una base egipcia de Timbaland (1999), por no parecer neoyorquino ante los suyos: le dio doce compases y no fue a Trinidad al vídeo, pero los catapultó a todo el mundo. Encarcelado de 2002 a 2005, volvió con Underground Kingz (2007), número 1, y murió ese diciembre. «Keeping it trill» fue su legado. A mediados de los 2000 llegó la ola de Houston: Slim Thug, Paul Wall, Chamillionaire, Mike Jones, Swishahouse y «Still Tippin’»; Bun B avaló a Drake en «Uptown» (2009), por la fe de Jas Prince.

refs.q: That was a big thing for Pimp, not wanting to do the song because he didn’t want people who had never heard of UGK to have a distorted view of who we were and what we represented.
refs.para: Bun B (artist, UGK): That was a big thing for Pimp, not wanting to do the song because he didn’t want people who had never heard of UGK to have a distorted view of who we were and what we represented.
refs.chapter: Cap. 18: The South Got Something to Say

refs.para: We don’t have that. It’s a different struggle. He definitely represents the underdog: If you put your mind to it, you can do it. Don’t be a clone. Fuck the clones. There’s no sense of being a clone. Be yourself. That’s what he was basically saying. Be yourself. There’s only one you. Keeping it trill. That’s a lifestyle. If people don’t understand what it is, it’s too real. I think keeping it trill is definitely one of his legacies. Being proud of who you are and going for yours.
refs.chapter: Cap. 18: The South Got Something to Say

refs.q: Southern hospitality is a trait for many of us here.
refs.para: Bun B (artist, UGK): Southern hospitality is a trait for many of us here. There’s a very easygoingness about our lifestyle, our character, and our demeanor that people relate to. It’s very personable.
